title: Iulii Firmici Iunioris Mathesis
shelf_note: A 15th-century humanist-cursive manuscript of Firmicus Maternus' Mathesis. This page is the model nativities of Demosthenes, Homer and Plato (Book VI). No tradition or collection is set, so there is nothing for it to contradict. The display title says 'second copy', so a check for a duplicate record of the work is worth doing.
structure_note: The 'VI' at the head of the leaf is the book's running head (Mathesis Book VI), not a folio. The OCR tags it <page-num>VI</page-num>. A running head repeating across a book's leaves explains most of the 46 printed_repeats and 49 backsteps among the 169 'printed numbers', so this is mis-tagged page furniture, not a broken sequence. The structure counts give pages_translated 0, but pages_translated_field gives 302 and this page has a translation, so one of the two counters is wrong.

pages.layout: single column of humanist cursive; rubricated (red) marginal notes in the outer left margin naming the nativities; paragraph brackets in the left margin; faint later marginalia and show-through

ocr_errors.ocr: An animo mesto cupiditatis ardore prorepserit
ocr_errors.image: ista coniunctio incesto cupiditatis ardore sorores suas
ocr_errors.problem: The clause on the image is about incest ('this conjunction, by incestuous heat of desire, makes them take their sisters as wives'). It is misread as unrelated words, and the subject of the prediction is lost.
Taurus is misread as 'Jupiter's sign'. This is a planetary placement in Demosthenes' model nativity.

ocr_errors.problem: Capricorn, the Sun's sign in Homer's nativity, is misread as 'equo'. The zodiac sign is lost.
'is found in a feminine sign' becomes 'is in the same sign'

other.note: The OCR tags the running head 'VI' (book number) as <page-num>, which corrupts the printed-number counts
<meta> asserts what the previous page contained ('the Sun does not see the ascendant'); this cannot be checked from this leaf

items.quote: the place rising next after the ascendant

missing.why: the 'trine' aspect (planets 120° apart) is not explained, and the configurations depend on it
'terms' (fines) is a technical division of each sign assigned to a planet, unknown to a general reader
'the eighth' means the eighth house/place from the ascendant; the house system is never glossed
'diameter' means opposition (180°), which a reader will not guess

missing.english: joined to the ascendant by exact radiation
missing.why: 'exact' (partilis) aspect, to the degree, is a technical term

book_verdict: A real Firmicus manuscript on the right shelf. The cursive is misread at several hinge points, though: an incest prediction becomes ordinary marriage, and two zodiac placements in the model nativities of Demosthenes and Homer are wrong. The fluent English carries all of these errors. The running head 'VI' is mis-tagged as a page number.
